samples.name: Amoxicillin 500mg Capsules (Antibiotic)
samples.text:
PACKAGE LEAFLET: INFORMATION FOR THE USER
Amoxicillin 500mg Hard Capsules

1. WHAT AMOXICILLIN IS AND WHAT IT IS USED FOR
Amoxicillin is an antibiotic. It belongs to a group of medicines called 'penicillins'. It is used to treat infections caused by bacteria in different parts of the body, such as chest infections (bronchitis or pneumonia), dental abscesses, and urinary tract infections.

2. BEFORE YOU TAKE AMOXICILLIN
Do not take Amoxicillin if you are allergic (hypersensitive) to amoxicillin, penicillin or any of the other ingredients of this medicine, or if you have ever had an allergic reaction to any antibiotic.
Warnings and precautions:
Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking Amoxicillin if you have kidney problems, glandular fever, or are not urinating regularly.
Pregnancy and breast-feeding:
If you are pregnant or breast-feeding, think you may be pregnant or are planning to have a baby, ask your doctor or pharmacist for advice before taking this medicine.
Driving and using machines:
Amoxicillin can cause side effects and symptoms that may make you unfit to drive. Do not drive or use machines unless you are feeling well.

3. HOW TO TAKE AMOXICILLIN
Always take this medicine exactly as your doctor or pharmacist has told you. The usual dose for adults and elderly patients is 250 mg to 500 mg three times a day. Swallow the capsules whole with water at spaced intervals during the day. Do not chew or break open the capsules. Continue taking this medicine until the course is finished, even if you feel better.

4. POSSIBLE SIDE EFFECTS
Like all medicines, this medicine can cause side effects, although not everybody gets them.
Common side effects (may affect up to 1 in 10 people): Skin rash, feeling sick (nausea), diarrhoea.
Serious side effects - stop taking Amoxicillin and see a doctor straight away if you get:
Allergic reactions such as itching of the skin or hives (urticaria), swelling of the face, lips, tongue or body, or difficulty in breathing. Severe watery diarrhoea with bleeding, or blistering of the skin, eyes or mouth.

samples.name: Paracetamol 500mg Tablets (Pain Reliever)
samples.text:
PACKAGE LEAFLET: INFORMATION FOR THE USER
Paracetamol 500 mg Tablets
Paracetamol

1. What Paracetamol Tablets are and what they are used for
Paracetamol is an analgesic (painkiller) and antipyretic (reduces body temperature when you have a fever). Paracetamol Tablets are used to relieve mild to moderate pain including headache, migraine, toothache, period pain, backache, rheumatic aches and muscular pains, and to relieve symptoms of colds and flu and sore throat.

2. What you need to know before you take Paracetamol Tablets
Do not take Paracetamol Tablets if you are allergic to paracetamol or any of the other ingredients. Do not take with any other paracetamol-containing products.
Warnings and precautions:
Do not exceed the stated dose. Immediate medical advice should be sought in the event of an overdose, even if you feel well, because of the risk of delayed serious liver damage.
Talk to your doctor if you have severe kidney or liver disease, or chronic alcoholism.
Pregnancy and breast-feeding:
If necessary, Paracetamol can be used during pregnancy. You should use the lowest possible dose that reduces your pain and/or your fever and use it for the shortest time possible. If you are breast-feeding, consult your doctor.

3. How to take Paracetamol Tablets
Adults, the elderly and young persons aged 16 and over: Take 1 or 2 tablets with water every 4 to 6 hours as required. Do not take more than 8 tablets (4000 mg) in 24 hours. Children aged 10 to 15 years: Take 1 tablet every 4 to 6 hours as required. Do not take more than 4 tablets in 24 hours. Not recommended for children under 10 years.

4. Possible side effects
Side effects with paracetamol are rare. However, severe skin reactions, blood disorders, and allergic reactions (such as skin rashes or swelling) have been reported very rarely. If you experience unexpected bruising or bleeding, stop taking the tablets and consult a doctor immediately.

samples.name: Ibuprofen 400mg Film-Coated Tablets (Anti-inflammatory)
samples.text:
PATIENT INFORMATION LEAFLET
Ibuprofen 400mg Tablets

What this medicine is for:
Ibuprofen belongs to a group of medicines known as Non-Steroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs (NSAIDs). It works by changing how the body responds to pain, swelling and high temperature. Used for the relief of headaches, dental pain, period pain, muscular pain, backache, and fever.

Warnings - Do NOT take if:
- You have or have ever had a stomach ulcer, perforation or bleeding.
- You are allergic to ibuprofen or aspirin or other NSAIDs.
- You have severe heart failure, severe kidney failure or severe liver failure.
- You are in the last 3 months of pregnancy.
Avoid taking with alcohol as it can increase the risk of stomach bleeding.
May cause dizziness or drowsiness; if affected, do not drive or operate machinery.

How to take:
For oral administration and short-term use only. Adults and children over 12 years: Swallow 1 tablet whole with water, preferably with or after food, up to three times a day as needed. Leave at least 4 hours between doses. Do not take more than 3 tablets (1200mg) in 24 hours.

Possible side effects:
Common and mild: Indigestion (dyspepsia), heartburn, nausea, stomach pain, mild diarrhoea or constipation.
Serious side effects (seek urgent medical care): Vomiting blood, dark black sticky stools, shortness of breath, unexplained stomach pain, or allergic swelling of face and lips.

samples.name: Lisinopril 10mg Tablets (Blood Pressure)
samples.text:
PACKAGE LEAFLET: INFORMATION FOR THE USER
Lisinopril 10 mg Tablets

1. What Lisinopril is and what it is used for
Lisinopril belongs to a group of medicines called ACE inhibitors (angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors). It works by widening your blood vessels, which helps to lower your blood pressure and makes it easier for your heart to pump blood around your body. It is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and heart failure.

2. Before you take Lisinopril
Do not take Lisinopril if you are more than 3 months pregnant, if you have previously had an allergic reaction involving swelling of your hands, feet, ankles, face, lips, tongue or throat which caused difficulty in swallowing or breathing (angioedema), or if you have diabetes or impaired kidney function and you are treated with a blood pressure lowering medicine containing aliskiren.
Warnings: Drinking alcohol with this medicine may make you feel dizzy or light-headed. Talk to your doctor before driving or using tools.

3. How to take Lisinopril
Always take Lisinopril exactly as your doctor has told you. The usual starting dose for hypertension is 10 mg once daily. Swallow the tablet with a drink of water, at the same time each day, with or without food.

4. Possible side effects
Common side effects: Headache, feeling dizzy or light-headed especially when standing up quickly, persistent dry cough, diarrhea, vomiting.
Serious side effects: Severe allergic reaction with swelling of face, lips, tongue or throat, severe dizziness or fainting, yellowing of skin or eyes (jaundice).
